title: Upstream P0002 — action_rpg
prompt:
Create a polished Roblox creature-collecting adventure RPG inspired by the exploration, monster bonding, egg hatching, riding, crafting, and turn-based combat of creature-rider RPGs.

Everything must be original. Do not copy existing monster designs, names, locations, interfaces, music, characters, or storylines.

The player is a young Warden who explores a fantasy wilderness, finds creature eggs, hatches creatures called Wildkin, builds a party, crafts equipment, and investigates a magical corruption called the Shattering.

Create a playable vertical slice with:

* One central village.
* One large wilderness region.
* One small dungeon.
* Six original Wildkin species.
* A short introductory storyline.
* Turn-based battles.
* Egg collecting and hatching.
* Creature party management.
* Creature riding.
* Crafting and equipment.
* Saving and loading.
* PC, mobile, and controller support.

Prioritize functional gameplay over map size. Avoid placeholder buttons and unfinished systems.
evidence: "One central village," "One small dungeon," and "Use a small instanced dungeon entered from the wilderness" explicitly describe a safe hub/overworld feeding a separate instanced combat area. "crafting and equipment" and the compact progression loop also fit its town-and-grinding support options.
addendum:
LAYOUT FEATURES for this RPG map. Build these as the actual structure of the space rather than as set dressing, keep them visually distinct from one another, and keep the whole layout legible in one view.

SHAPE OF THE SPACE - Hub and Dungeons: A safe hub feeding separate instanced combat areas entered from the overworld.

INCLUDE:
- Sanctuary Town: A settlement completely isolated from enemy AI where players restock, repair, and turn in quests.
- Economy Ring: Shop, quest giver, and blacksmith clustered tightly together to cut repetitive travel for grinding players.
- Aggro Bowl: Wide open clearings or monster nests holding hostile spawns, set well back from travel roads so low-level players aren't ambushed in transit.

title: Upstream P0003 — action_rpg
prompt:
Create a massive, seamless 3D Open-World RPG map divided into 4 hyper-detailed mega-biomes, connected by a central neutral hub called "The Nexus Palace".

Zone 1 (Cyberpunk Metropolis): A dense neon-lit futuristic city. Add towering skyscrapers with holographic advertisements, drivable hover-car lanes in the sky, dark rainy asphalt streets with puddle reflections, and accessible underground cyberpunk slums filled with neon signs and rusty pipes.
Zone 2 (Mystical Luminescent Forest): A fantasy forest where everything glows. Generate giant ancient trees with glowing purple leaves, bioluminescent rivers flowing with neon blue water, interactive glowing mushrooms that boost player jump height, and dense volumetric fog floating between the trees.
Zone 3 (Scrapyard Wasteland): A post-apocalyptic diesel-punk desert. Fill it with moving sandstorms, massive rusted metal shipwrecks, turning mechanical gears half-buried in the sand, and abandoned scavenger outposts made of iron sheets.
Zone 4 (Celestial Floating Kingdom): A majestic realm of sky islands. Design white marble castles with gold trims, floating waterfalls that drop water into the endless sky, moving cloud 
platforms for parkour, and ancient Greek-style temples.

Implement an advanced, fluid, and responsive 3D movement and Combat System for all players.
Movement Mechanics: Enable smooth wall-running on flat vertical surfaces, a tactical double-dash with motion blur effects, a grappling hook system that attaches to any metal or wooden structure, and a ledge-climbing mechanic.
Combat Core: Build a hybrid combat system (Melee and Ranged). Melee weapons (like Laser Katanas and Greatswords) must have a 3-hit combo animation system with camera-shake on impact and directional slashing visual effects. Ranged weapons (like Plasma Rifles and Magic Staffs) must feature over-the-shoulder aiming, custom particle projectiles, projectile drop, and localized hitboxes (Headshot = 2.5x damage).
Class Skill Trees: Implement 3 distinct classes (Cyber-Ninja, Arch-Mage, and Wasteland Juggernaut), each with 5 unique unlockable active skills containing custom particle VFX.
Populate the map with smart Al enemies and 4 massive World Bosses,

.one for each biome

Minion Al: Enemies must use pathfinding to chase players, take cover behind walls when low on health, and alert nearby allies when

.engaged in combat

Cyber Metropolis Boss ("Mecha-Titan Prime"): A 50-foot-tall robot

that spawns in the city center. It shoots tracking homing missiles, slams the ground creating a massive expanding shockwave ring that players must jump over, and enters a shield-overcharge phase

.at 30% health

Floating Kingdom Boss ("Aether Dragon"): A massive flying dragon that circles the sky castles. It breathes holy fire that coats platforms in damaging light, creates tornadoes that push players off the floating islands, and requires players to use their grappling hooks to .board its back to deal critical damage

Script a global dynamic 24-minute Day/Night cycle combined with a .randomized Weather Engine that alters gameplay
Day/Night Cycle: Transition smoothly between a bright sunny day with God-rays, a golden hour sunset, and a pitch-black midnight .where players require flashlights or glowing gear to see
Dynamic Weather: Randomly trigger 4 weather events: Heavy Acid Rain in the Cyberpunk City (deals slowly chipping armor damage over time), Magic Mana Storm in the Forest (amplifies magic damage by 50% and changes sky color to purple), Sandstorm in the Wasteland (reduces player visibility to 15 studs and slows movement speed), and Thunderstorms in the Floating Kingdom (lightning bolts strike random spots on the map, causing instant .death if hit)

Create a comprehensive RPG data-store, inventory, and user interface framework.
UI Layout: Design a clean, modern, and minimalist sci-fi/fantasy hybrid GUI. Include a circular health and mana bar in the bottom center, a mini-map in the top-right showing quest markers and player locations, and a neat clean side-menu for Inventory, Skills, and Quests.
Loot & Inventory: Build a color-coded rarity system for drops (Common=White, Rare=Blue, Epic=Purple, Legendary=Gold). Items must drop from defeated enemies as physical glowing 3D crates that players can walk over to collect. Implement a full Inventory screen with weapon equipping slots and stat displays.
Data Persistence: Ensure all player data (Level, Gold, Gems, Equipped Items, Skill Tree Points) saves automatically using Roblox DataStoreService every 60 seconds and upon leaving the server.

extras.text: Include an accessible underground slum layer beneath the metropolis.
Provide moving cloud platforms as traversable parkour routes between the floating islands.

evidence: "massive, seamless 3D Open-World RPG map divided into 4 hyper-detailed mega-biomes" and "one continuous seamless surface"

- Island Cluster: Several separate landmasses with water or open air between them, crossed by bridge, boat, or flight.

prompt:
A truly "complete" massive game with every single detail would be millions of words-far larger than what can fit in a single response (it would be comparable to dozens of novels and professional game design documents).

Instead, here's the blueprint for a game that could realistically become a AAA-sized title.

Eclipse: Rise of the Eternal Kingdoms

Genre: Open-World MMORPG Action RPG + PvP + Story Quest Game

Players: 1-500,000 Online

Perspective: Third Person (Optional First Person)

STORY

Thousands of years ago...

The world was protected by the Eternal Core.

One day it shattered into seven fragments.

The fragments gave people incredible powers.

Kings fought over them.

Dark creatures known as the Hollow have returned.

Every player begins as an unknown adventurer.

1. نظام اللوبي والواجهات الرئيسية (Lobby & UI Systems)
أ. منطقة اللوبي (Main Lobby Hub)
التصميم: منطقة آمنة عائمة في الفضاء ذات تصميم مستقبلي (Futuristic Floating Citadel).
المحتويات في اللوبي:
بوابة بدء المتاهة (Dungeon Portal): بوابة نيون كبرى يتجمع فيها اللاعبون، تحتوي على مؤقت زمني 10 ثوانٍ لبدء المجموعات (Solo / Co-op حتى 4 لاعبين).
منطقة التدريب (Training Dummy Zone): دمية قتالية لا تموت باختبار الضرر (DPS Calculator).
منصة الإنجازات (Leaderboards): شاشات ثلاثية الأبعاد تعرض أعلى اللاعبين تقييماً وأسرع وقت لإنهاء الألغاز.
ب. القوائم والواجهات على الشاشة (HUD & UI Design)
الشاشة الرئيسية للاعب (Main HUD):
أعلى اليسار: شريط الصحة (HP) باللون الأخضر، شريط الطاقة/المانا (Energy) باللون الأزرق، ورقم المستوئ (Level).
أعلى اليمين: عرض العملات: الكريستال الأزرق (Blue Crystals) [عملة مجانية من اللعب] + الجوهر الذهبي (Gold Essence) [عملة نادرة].
أسفل المنتصف: شريط القدرات (Ability Bar) يعرض 4 خانات لمهارات السلاح والقدرات الخاصة مع وقت الانتظار (Cooldown Cooldown Icons).
أعلى المنتصف: بوصلة/مؤشر يوجه اللاعب باتجاه اللغز القادم أو موقع الأعداء.
2. القوائم الفرعية والمتجر (Menus & Shop System)
أ. قائمة المتجر (In-Game Shop UI)
تحتوي قائمة المتجر على 3 تبويبات رئيسية:
تبويب السكنات (Skins & Cosmetics):
سكنات الشخصيات (Character Auras & Suits): (مثل: سكن النيون الفضائي، سكن الحارس الفولاذي، سكن ظل النار). تغيير مظهر الشخصية وتأثير أقدامها عند المشي دون إعطاء ميزة تفوق (Cosmetic Only).
سكنات الأسلحة (Weapon Skins): تأثيرات سيوف متوهجة (مثل: السيف المشتعل، سيف البرق الأزرق).
تبويب الأسلحة والترقيات (Weapons & Upgrades):
شراء وتطوير الأسلحة الأساسية باستخدام الكريستال الأزرق (سيف القتال القريب، خنجر السرعة، مطرقة الضرر الجماعي).
تبويب المواد الاستهلاكية (Consumables):
مشروبات زيادة الصحة (Health Potions)، ومشروبات السرعة المؤقتة (Speed Boosts).
ب. قائمة القدرات وشجرة المهارات (Abilities & Skill Tree)
يمتلك كل لاعب 3 قدرات رئيسية قابلة للتثبيت والتطوير:
القدرة 1: اندفاع البرق (Dash/Teleport): تتيح للاعب الاندفاع للأمام بسرعة وتفادي ضربات الأعداء أو فخاخ الألغاز (وقت الانتظار: 5 ثوانٍ).
القدرة 2: درع الحماية (Pulse Shield): درع ضوئي امتصاصي لمدة 3 ثوانٍ يعكس جزءاً من ضرر المقذوفات (وقت الانتظار: 12 ثانية).
القدرة 3: المهارة القصوى - موجة الصدمة (Ultimate: Shockwave): ضرب الأرض بقوة لتجميد جميع الأعداء في النطاق لمدة 3 ثوانٍ وحل الألغاز المعتمدة على الضغط السريع (وقت الانتظار: 45 ثانية).
3. تفاصيل ماب اللعب والمراحل (Gameplay Map Details)
عند دخول البوابة، ينزل اللاعب إلى متاهة قلعة الآلات (Crystal Citadel) وتتكون من 3 مناطق تفصيلية:
المنطقة الأولى: ساحة الأبراج والرموز
المظهر: ساحة مغلقة بحوائط حجرية سوداء وتوجد 4 أعمدة كريستالية ملونة.
طريقة اللعب:
رسبنة 20 وحش حراسة (Minion Bots).
عند القضاء عليهم، تظهر إشارة ضوئية على الجدار بترتيب الألوان.
تفعيل الأزرار بالترتيب الصحيح يفتح البوابة الكبرى ويفيض بالذهب والكريستال.
المنطقة الثانية: غرفة الليزر والمتاهة المتحركة
المظهر: أرضية من مكعبات متغيرة الارتفاع مع أشعة ليزر حمراء متحركة أفقياً وعمودياً.
طريقة اللعب:
استخدام مهارة الاندفاع (Dash) لتفادي أشعة الليزر.
العثور على 3 مفاتيح طاقة مجسمة مخبأة خلف مكعبات الأرضية المتحركة وتوصيلها باللوحة المركزية أثناء التصدي للوحوش الطائرة.
المنطقة الثالثة: عرش الزعيم الكريستالي (The Final Boss)
المظهر: صالة عرش ضخمة جداً مع أرضية زجاجية تحتها حمم بركانية نيونية.
طريقة القتال واللغز:
الزعيم محمي بموجة طاقة غير قابلة للكسر.
على الأرض توجد 4 دوائر ضغط ضوئية (Pressure Plates).
يجب على اللاعب استدراج الزعيم ليقف فوق الدائرة المضيئة ثم ضربها لتفعيل فخ يسقط درع الزعيم لمدة 6 ثوانٍ، وهنا يمكن ضربه وإلحاق الضرر الفعلي به.
عند وصول صحة الزعيم إلى 25%، يدخل في حالة "الغضب" وتتضاعف سرعة هجماته ويصبح المطلوب توقيت القفز والتفادي بدقة عالية.
4. ميكانيكيات النظام والبرمجة (System Mechanics)
نظام المكافآت وتجربة اللاعب (XP & Loot System):
إنهاء الماب يعطي خبرة (XP) لرفع مستوى الحساب وتكافئ اللاعب بـ 500 كريستال أزرق.
نظام إعادة الترسبن (Respawn & Checkpoints):
توجد نقاط حفظ تلقائية (Checkpoints) عند بداية كل منطقة. عند موت اللاعب يعاد ترسبنه في نقطة الحفظ السابقة دون خسارة تقدم الألغاز.
الصوتيات والتأثيرات (Audio & SFX):
أصوات واضحة للتفاعل مع الأزرار والمتاجر، ومؤثرات صوتية مميزة لكل مهارة، مع موسيقى حماسية تتغير حسب وتيرة القتال.

title: Upstream P0013 — action_rpg
prompt:
Executive Summary
Create a Roblox Demonfall-inspired open-world action RPG set in a Taishō-era fantasy. The player starts as a human in a rural earth-biome village, returns home to find their family slain by a demon, then splinters into two paths: Survive = become a Slayer, Die = become a Demon. A cinematic prologue and mobile-friendly obby tutorial teach basic movement (run, jump, camera), combat (light/heavy attack, block, dash), and UI (controls overlay before drawing the katana). Players choose a family (clan) with unique buffs and cosmetic style during character creation (e.g. Kanroji clan gives +15% damage, Kamado clan +20% EXP and Sun-immunity). The core gameplay loop emphasizes dynamic combat with stamina/breathing management, deep progression (skill tree, breathing styles, Blood Demon Arts), cooperative PvE missions (with scalable difficulty), and a day/night cycle that makes nights dangerous (demons hunt; they die in daylight without Sun immunity).

Key Systems:

Combat: Simple mobile controls (touch buttons) and PC controls (keyboard/mouse) for light/heavy slash, block, dash/sprint, weapon draw/sheath, plus a visible Stamina/Breath meter. Advanced skills are unlocked via breathing styles (9-12 styles) or demon arts.
Progression: Players earn skill points by killing demons, completing quests, and conquering missions. A branching skill tree lets them improve stats (Strength, Endurance, Speed, Steel-Lungs to slow breathing drain, Dash upgrades, etc.) and unlock special moves.
Breathing Styles (Slayer paths): At least ten breathing arts (Water, Flame, Thunder, Wind, Mist, Stone, Love, Serpent, Sound, Beast, plus secret Sun/Moon) exist, each with trainer NPCs and unlock quests. Four beginner-friendly styles (Water, Flame, Thunder, Beast) are accessible early; higher-tier styles require harder quests or demos. Demon Path and Transformations
If the player's prologue "boss" demon wins, the player becomes a Demon. Demons have: auto HP regen, extra mobility, and unique Blood Arts (special skills). The demon progression ladder is:

Minor Demons (random spawns, weaker).
Demon Ranks 1-10 (named demonic fighters).
Lower Moon Bosses 6-1.
Upper Moon Bosses 5-1 (team raids).
Muzan (Ultimate Demon Lord) optional endgame fight.
Players can switch sides mid-game:

A Slayer → Demon requires Muzan's Blood (quest reward or rare merchant item) and a timed "corruption" (24 real-hours that can speed up with level). High-level Slayers (w/ breathing) become a Hybrid demon (Sun-breathing enabled, lore nod to Kokushibo/Kyogai).
A Demon → Slayer can happen via a Wipe Potion (sold by a rare NPC for high cost, or via achievement/quest), which resets your demon state and lets you join the Corps. Demons get exclusive quests (hunt high-value humans, ambush missions) and rewards (demon points, Blood Demon Art unlocks).
Death in normal play is lenient: players simply respawn at their chosen village spawn point with slight penalties (lost time only). Only the introductory fight converts the character.

Quest and Mission System
Missions are accepted from quest boards or NPCs in villages. They auto-complete for party members. Major mission types:

Hunt Missions: Kill X demons in region.
Defense Missions: Defend an NPC/building from waves.
Escort Missions: Protect a villager or merchant.
Investigation Missions: Solve a mystery (find missing person, track demon tracks).
Boss Missions: Unlock and fight a specific Lower/Upper Moon boss (requires group).
Survival Missions: Survive a time period on Demon-infested road.
Dungeon Raids: Clear an enemy camp/cave for loot.
A mission UI lets players select, track progress, and see rewards (currency, XP, skill points, special items).

Boss Ladder
Design bosses in tiers, reflecting Demonfall's Lower/Upper Moons. At least include Lower Moon 6→1, Upper Moon 5→1, plus optional Hashira rivals. Each boss has unique mechanics (e.g. blind spots, minion adds, stage phases). Key bosses: Spider Demon (Lower 6), Bountiful Demon (multi-boss Lower 5), (Lower 1-3 as in series), then Upper Moons like Nakime (teleport map), Gyokko (water demon), Kokushibo (endgame hybrid boss), Muzan (final final). Defeating each yields rare drops (unique abilities or crafting mats).

Spawn/Revival Screen: Let player set their spawn village (applied each death).

Skill Tree UI: Grid with nodes (Breath styles, Strength, Stamina, special moves). Tapping a node shows name, description, cost in points. Branching tree lines. Accessible via menu.

Breathing Styles Screen: List unlocked styles and locked ones (with "How to unlock" tips).

Quest Log: Scrollable list of active/available quests, with objectives and map markers.

Create a Roblox Demonfall-inspired open-world action RPG set in a Taishō-era fantasy. The player starts as a human in a rural earth-biome village, returns home to find their family slain by a demon, then splinters into two paths: Survive = become a Slayer, Die = become a Demon. A cinematic prologue and mobile-friendly obby tutorial teach basic movement (run, jump, camera), combat (light/heavy attack, block, dash), and UI (controls overlay before drawing the katana). Players choose a family (clan) with unique buffs and cosmetic style during character creation (e.g. Kanroji clan gives +15% damage, Kamado clan +20% EXP and Sun-immunity). The core gameplay loop emphasizes dynamic combat with stamina/breathing management, deep progression (skill tree, breathing styles, Blood Demon Arts), cooperative PvE missions (with scalable difficulty), and a day/night cycle that makes nights dangerous (demons hunt; they die in daylight without Sun immunity).

Key Systems:

Combat: Simple mobile controls (touch buttons) and PC controls (keyboard/mouse) for light/heavy slash, block, dash/sprint, weapon draw/sheath, plus a visible Stamina/Breath meter. Advanced skills are unlocked via breathing styles (9-12 styles) or demon arts.
Progression: Players earn skill points by killing demons, completing quests, and conquering missions. A branching skill tree lets them improve stats (Strength, Endurance, Speed, Steel-Lungs to slow breathing drain, Dash upgrades, etc.) and unlock special moves.
Breathing Styles (Slayer paths): At least ten breathing arts (Water, Flame, Thunder, Wind, Mist, Stone, Love, Serpent, Sound, Beast, plus secret Sun/Moon) exist, each with trainer NPCs and unlock quests. Four beginner-friendly styles (Water, Flame, Thunder, Beast) are accessible early; higher-tier styles require harder quests or demos. For example, Beast Breathing (dual-wield style) requires Level 10, 10,000 Yen, dual katanas and a hidden mountain cave trainer. Clan synergy is important: e.g., Hashibira clan grants +10% damage for Beast users.
Demon Path: If a player dies in the prologue, they become a demon with regeneration, Blood Arts, and increased power. Demons climb their own boss ladder (ordinary demons → Demon Ranks → Lower Moon bosses → Upper Moon bosses). Slayer players may choose to become demons by consuming Muzan's blood (a rare item or boss drop) and waiting in "hybrid" limbo (taking real-time hours based on level). Conversely, demons can revert via a rare Wipe Potion sold by a special merchant, or by codes, reflecting community lore.
World & Quests: A large open map (see World Map diagram below) connects varied zones: the Starting Village (tutorial area), Cursed Forests (moonlit wood with fog), Snowy Mountain Pass (Beast trainer), Butterfly Mansion (advanced training/Full Concentration skill), Swordsmith Village/Forge, Haunted Roads (night raids), Spider Mountain Caves (elite slayer boss), and an Endgame Fortress (final raids). Day/night cycles and weather (fog, rain, moonlight) dynamically affect visibility and demon behavior. NPCs follow schedules (working/closing shops in day, hiding at night), and random events (e.g. demon attacks on a caravan, lost child rescues, or chance boss spawns) create a living world. Quests include daily hunts, escort/defense missions, boss investigations, and special trials. Party missions auto-scale: more players = tougher enemies and better rewards.
Building & Tech: The design is modular for Roblox Build. We define core modules (Combat, Movement, UI, etc.) and RemoteEvents for communication. Development is phased: 1) Foundation: world base, controls, spawn points, character/family selection, tutorial obby. 2) Core Combat: weapon equip, attacks, block, dodge, enemy AI, stamina. 3) Progression & Quests: skill tree, breathing trainers, basic quests, party system. 4) World Expansion: add villages, NPCs, day/night, weather, merchant, Butterfly Mansion. 5) Endgame: boss fights (Lower/Upper Moons, Hashira mentors), transformation routes, secret rewards. 6) Polish: UI/UX, effects, sound/music, performance tweaks (especially mobile).

Day/Night Cycle: Demonfall had a day/night cycle reinstated. Here, night strengthens demons (higher spawn rate, they gain stealth). Demons (without Sun immunity) take damage or die in daylight, so survivors flee or burn at dawn. Weather effects (rain reduces visibility, heavy fog delays sight) add tactical depth. ⚔️ ROBLOX FIGHTING SIMULATOR - FULL GAME PLAN

🎮 GAME IDEA

A fast-paced fighting simulator where players train stats, unlock abilities, and battle other players or bosses to become the strongest.

---

🧠 CORE GAME LOOP

1. Spawn in lobby
2. Train stats (Strength, Speed, Defense, Energy)
3. Fight NPCs or players
4. Earn coins + XP
5. Unlock new zones, powers, and gear
6. Repeat → get stronger → dominate

---

💪 STATS SYSTEM

Each player has:

- Strength → increases damage
- Speed → increases attack speed + movement
- Defense → reduces damage taken
- Energy → used for abilities

👉 Training methods:

- Punching (Strength)
- Running (Speed)
- Taking hits (Defense)
- Charging aura (Energy)

---

🗺️ MAP / ZONES

Create multiple areas players unlock:

1. Beginner Arena (starter)
2. City Streets
3. Dojo
4. Lava Arena
5. Space Zone
6. God Arena (endgame)

👉 Each zone:

- Stronger enemies
- Better rewards
- Access locked by stat requirements

---

👊 COMBAT SYSTEM

Basic attacks:

- Click = punch combo (1-2-3 hits)
- Heavy attack (cooldown)

Advanced:

- Block (reduces damage)
- Dash (quick movement)
- Combo system (more hits = bonus damage)

---

🔥 ABILITIES SYSTEM

Players unlock abilities:

- Energy Blast
- Dash Strike
- Ground Smash
- Lightning Punch
- Ultimate Mode (temporary power boost)

👉 Add cooldowns + flashy effects

---

🧍 NPC ENEMIES

Add enemies in each zone:

- Weak Dummy
- Street Fighter
- Ninja
- Lava Monster
- Space Warrior
- Final Boss

👉 Bosses:

- Huge HP
- Special attacks
- Drop rare rewards

---

💰 REWARDS SYSTEM

Players earn:

- Coins (main currency)
- Gems (rare currency)
- XP (level up)

Use coins for:

- Upgrades
- Abilities
- New zones

---

🛒 SHOP SYSTEM

Shop should include:

- Stat multipliers (x2 strength, etc.)
- Ability unlocks
- Cosmetic auras
- Titles

---

🎒 INVENTORY SYSTEM

Players can equip:

- Auras (visual power)
- Trails
- Titles
- Effects

---

🧬 PROGRESSION SYSTEM

Level system:

- Gain XP from fights
- Level up = stat boosts

Rebirth system:

- Reset stats
- Gain permanent multiplier

---

⚡ UI SYSTEM (MAKE THIS INSANE)

Must include:

- Health bar (animated)
- Energy bar
- Damage numbers (floating)
- Combo counter
- Ability hotbar
- Shop UI (smooth + glowing)
- Level display

---

🏆 MULTIPLAYER SYSTEM

- PvP arenas
- Safe zones (no fighting)
- Leaderboards:
 - Top strength
 - Top kills
 - Top rebirths

---

🎆 EFFECTS (VERY IMPORTANT)

Add:

- Punch impact effects
- Explosion VFX
- Energy beams
- Screen shake
- Glow auras

👉 This makes the game feel HIGH QUALITY

---

🎯 EXTRA FEATURES (TO GO VIRAL)

- Daily rewards
- Spin wheel rewards
- Quests system
- Trading system
- Gamepasses (2x stats, auto train)

---

🚀 UPDATE IDEAS

- New zones
- New abilities
- New bosses
- Limited-time events
- New aura effects

---

💡 SUCCESS TIP

Focus on:

- Smooth combat
- Flashy effects
- Addicting progression

If it FEELS powerful → players stay.

---

title: Upstream P0068 — board_card_games
prompt:
# Prompt: Real-Time Settlers-style Roblox Game

Build a Roblox multiplayer strategy game in Luau, inspired by Settlers of Catan, with three core rule changes from the original: no dice, real-time play instead of turns, and no resource storage caps. Below is the full spec.

## Core Concept
A hex-grid resource/settlement game where players build roads, settlements, and cities using resources that accumulate automatically over time from hexes they're adjacent to. There are no turns and no dice - the game is a continuous, real-time economy race.

## Rule Changes & Why They Matter for Implementation

**1. No dice - production comes from hex "tiers"**
- Each hex has a fixed production rate instead of a dice-roll number token.
- Make tiers visually intuitive without needing a legend: e.g., hex size/height, glow intensity, or particle density scales with output rate. A player should be able to glance at the board and know a taller/brighter hex produces more, without reading a number.

=== spec.md ===
Title: Settlers (Catan-style Hex Board Game, Server-Authoritative)
Genre: Turn-Based Strategy / Resource Management Board Game
Platform: Roblox (Luau), single CAS build; 3D hex board + ScreenGui HUD, mobile-friendly

## 1. Global Settings & Architecture
- Players: up to 4 seats (hot-seat on one client, or multiplayer). Minimum viable: 2-4 players cycling turns on one device.
- Authority: Server owns the board, dice, all resource/structure state, turn order, robber, and rule validation (prevents illegal placements/rolls). Client renders the board + HUD and forwards intents.
- Networking: `RemoteEvent` `RollDice`; `RemoteEvent` `PlaceStructure` (args `kind` "settlement"|"city"|"road", `nodeOrEdgeId`); `RemoteEvent` `MoveRobber` (args `tileId`, optional `victimSeat`); `RemoteEvent` `EndTurn`; `RemoteEvent` `StateSync` (server -> client: board, players' resources, structures, turn, phase, lastRoll, robberTile).
- Camera: `Scriptable`, angled top-down over the board, static.

## 2. Board Model (Hex Grid)
- Standard 19-tile hex island (radii 1-2-3-2-1 rows: 3,4,5,4,3 tiles).
- Tile fields: `tileId` 1..19, `resource` ("wood"|"brick"|"sheep"|"wheat"|"ore"|"desert"), `numberToken` (2..12 excluding 7; desert has none), `hasRobber` (bool).
- Resource distribution: 4 wood, 3 brick, 4 sheep, 4 wheat, 3 ore, 1 desert (18 producing + desert). Number tokens: standard set 2,3,3,4,4,5,5,6,6,8,8,9,9,10,10,11,11,12 assigned to non-desert tiles.
- Tile colors: wood/forest #2E7D32, brick #C0562B, sheep #9CCC65, wheat #F4C430, ore #78909C, desert #D8C79A.
- Graph: 54 vertices (settlement/city nodes) and 72 edges (road slots) derived from the hex layout; each vertex stores adjacent tiles (for resource yield) and adjacent vertices (for distance rule); each edge stores its two endpoint vertices.

## 3. Turn Structure & Phases
- Setup phase: snake-order initial placement - each player places 2 settlements + 2 roads (2nd settlement grants starting resources from adjacent tiles). Enforced before main play.
- Main turn sequence per active player:
 1. `roll` - must `RollDice` first (2d6).
 2. `produce/robber` - resolve the roll (Section 5).
 3. `build` - optionally place roads/settlements/cities and/or trade.
 4. `EndTurn` - advance to next seat.
- `currentSeat` cycles 1→2→...→N→1. Only the active seat may act; the server rejects actions from other seats or out-of-phase actions.

## 4. Dice Roll
- `RollDice`: server generates two independent d6 (1..6 each), sum 2..12, sets `lastRoll`, animates dice, and applies the outcome (Section 5). Only allowed in `roll` phase for the active player; produces a visible value reflected in state within 5s.

## 5. Resource Production & Robber
- Non-7 roll: every tile whose `numberToken == roll` and does NOT have the robber produces its resource for each settlement (×1) or city (×2) on its adjacent vertices; resources added to the owning players. This can award resources to multiple players in one roll.
- Roll of 7 (robber): NO normal production. Instead:
 1. Every player with > 7 resource cards discards half (rounded down).
 2. The active player must `MoveRobber` to a different tile; that tile is blocked (produces nothing while robbed).
 3. The active player steals 1 random resource from a player with a structure adjacent to the new robber tile (if any).
- Robber state (`robberTile`) is authoritative and visualized by a robber pawn on the tile.

## 6. Building Costs & Rules
- Costs: Road = 1 wood + 1 brick; Settlement = 1 wood + 1 brick + 1 sheep + 1 wheat; City = 2 wheat + 3 ore (upgrades an existing settlement).
- On `PlaceStructure`, server validates and rejects if any fail:
 - Sufficient resources for the cost (else reject: insufficient resources).
 - Settlement: target vertex empty AND satisfies the distance rule (no settlement/city on any directly adjacent vertex) AND (after setup) connected to the player's own road.
 - Road: target edge empty AND connected to the player's own existing road/settlement/city.
 - City: target vertex currently holds the player's own settlement (upgrades it).
- On success: deduct cost, register the structure to the seat, broadcast StateSync. Points: settlement = 1 VP, city = 2 VP. First to 10 VP wins.

## 7. User Interface (UI) & HUD - ScreenGui layout
Root: `ScreenGui` (IgnoreGuiInset=true).
- Top Center (Turn): "TurnLabel" "Player 2's Turn" in that player's color, TextSize 30 `GothamBold`, anchor (0.5,0)+(0,12).
- Top Left (Last Roll): "RollLabel" showing two dice faces + sum, TextSize 28.
- Bottom (Resource Bar `ResourceBar`): full-width, height 96px, #1E1230 85%; 5 resource counters (Wood/Brick/Sheep/Wheat/Ore) with icon + count via `UIListLayout`, for the ACTIVE player. Counts update live.
- Bottom Right (Action buttons): "RollButton" (visible in roll phase), "BuildSettlement"/"BuildRoad"/"BuildCity" toggle buttons (build phase), "EndTurnButton". Laid out in a `UIListLayout`; if crowded, a `ScrollingFrame` keeps every action reachable.
- Build mode: selecting "BuildSettlement/Road/City" highlights all LEGAL vertices/edges (translucent #FFD93D markers); tapping a marker confirms placement.
- Victory Point tracker: small per-player VP chips top-right.
- Game Over overlay: "Player N Wins!" + Restart.
- Layout safety: turn/roll in top 72px, resource bar + actions in bottom ~150px, board in the middle; scroll ensures no counter/action clipped or off-screen.

## 8. Input & Screen-to-Board Mapping
- Placement uses discrete legal-target markers: in build mode the server sends the set of legal vertex/edge ids; the client shows a marker at each. A tap raycasts (`Camera:ScreenPointToRay`) and selects the nearest legal marker within 3 studs of the hit → `PlaceStructure(kind, id)`. Because each vertex/edge has a distinct marker and the ray uses the exact tapped pixel, the structure is placed at the tapped board location (intended vertex/edge), not a neighbor.
- Dice: tapping RollButton (a discrete `TextButton`) fires `RollDice`.
- Server re-validates every placement (Section 6) regardless of client markers, so illegal taps are rejected.

## 9. Audio
- `dice_roll.mp3` (0.5); `build.mp3` (0.5) on placement; `resource_gain.mp3` (0.4) on production; `robber.mp3` (0.5) on a 7; `steal.mp3` (0.4); `turn_change.mp3` (0.3); `victory.mp3` (0.6). Client-side.

## 10. Visual Style & Polish
- Palette: tiles per Section 2; player colors P1 #E74C3C, P2 #3498DB, P3 #F1C40F, P4 #2ECC71; legal-target markers #FFD93D; robber pawn #2C2C2C.
- Dice: 3D tumble animation settling on the rolled faces (0.6s).
- Settlement/city meshes in player color; roads as colored bars along edges.
- Number tokens: circular tiles with the number; 6 and 8 rendered in red (high-probability), others black.
- Resource gain: floating "+1 wood" text over producing vertices.

## 11. Roblox Feasibility Notes
- `ServerScriptService/CatanServer` holds the board graph (precomputed 19 tiles / 54 vertices / 72 edges adjacency), rules, and turn state; `StarterPlayerScripts/CatanClient` renders the board and HUD and does ScreenPointToRay placement. Turn-based → StateSync only on changes. Board graph is precomputed data (no runtime geometry solving). Scope (single island, core rules, no trading UI beyond bank optional) is realistic for one CAS build. Discrete markers make placement mobile-friendly.

## 12. Acceptance Criteria (maps 1:1 to test_plan core + advanced items)
- **AC-play_starts (core):** On Play, within 10s a hex board with resource tiles + number tokens AND a player/resource HUD are visible with no startup errors. (Sections 2, 7.)
- **AC-roll_dice (core):** A dice roll (2d6) produces a visible value and updates game state within 5s (only in roll phase for the active player). (Sections 3, 4.)
- **AC-place_settlement_road (core):** A settlement and/or road is placed at a valid vertex/edge and registered in state; invalid placements are rejected. (Sections 6, 8.)
- **AC-resources_and_turns (advanced):** After a roll, resources are awarded to players by adjacent structures on matching tiles, and EndTurn advances currentSeat to a different player. (Sections 3, 5.)
- **AC-robber_on_seven (advanced):** Rolling a 7 triggers the robber (no normal production; over-limit discards; robber moves/blocks a tile; steal) rather than distributing resources. (Section 5.)
- **AC-building_costs_and_rules (advanced):** Building deducts the correct cost AND illegal placements (insufficient resources or violating adjacency/distance/connectivity) are rejected. (Section 6.)
- **AC-input_mapping (advanced):** Discrete legal-target markers + exact-pixel raycast mean a settlement/road is placed at the tapped vertex/edge, not a neighbor. (Section 8.)
- **AC-no_runtime_errors (core):** Server validates seat/phase/cost/adjacency and uses a precomputed bounds-safe graph; no red console output. (Sections 3, 6, 11.)
- **AC-ui_layout_quality (polish):** Turn/roll (top 72px), resource bar + actions (bottom ~150px) never overlap and stay on-screen; scroll prevents clipping. (Section 7.)
- **AC-gameplay_clarity (polish):** Whose turn it is, the active player's resources, and available actions (roll/build/end) are clear from the HUD with no wall-of-text. (Section 7.)

- Standard 19-tile hex island (radii 1-2-3-2-1 rows: 3,4,5,4,3 tiles).
- Tile fields: `tileId` 1..19, `resource` ("wood"|"brick"|"sheep"|"wheat"|"ore"|"desert"), `numberToken` (2..12 excluding 7; desert has none), `hasRobber` (bool).
- Resource distribution: 4 wood, 3 brick, 4 sheep, 4 wheat, 3 ore, 1 desert (18 producing + desert). Number tokens: standard set 2,3,3,4,4,5,5,6,6,8,8,9,9,10,10,11,11,12 assigned to non-desert tiles.
- Tile colors: wood/forest #2E7D32, brick #C0562B, sheep #9CCC65, wheat #F4C430, ore #78909C, desert #D8C79A.
- Graph: 54 vertices (settlement/city nodes) and 72 edges (road slots) derived from the hex layout; each vertex stores adjacent tiles (for resource yield) and adjacent vertices (for distance rule); each edge stores its two endpoint vertices.

## 3. Turn Structure & Phases
- Setup phase: snake-order initial placement - each player places 2 settlements + 2 roads (2nd settlement grants starting resources from adjacent tiles). Enforced before main play.
- Main turn sequence per active player:
 1. `roll` - must `RollDice` first (2d6).
 2. `produce/robber` - resolve the roll (Section 5).
 3. `build` - optionally place roads/settlements/cities and/or trade.
 4. `EndTurn` - advance to next seat.
- `currentSeat` cycles 1→2→...→N→1. Only the active seat may act; the server rejects actions from other seats or out-of-phase actions.

## 4. Dice Roll
- `RollDice`: server generates two independent d6 (1..6 each), sum 2..12, sets `lastRoll`, animates dice, and applies the outcome (Section 5). Only allowed in `roll` phase for the active player; produces a visible value reflected in state within 5s.

 - Road: target edge empty AND connected to the player's own existing road/settlement/city.

- Game Over overlay: "Player N Wins!" + Restart.

prompt:
Roblox Grand Strategy Game Design

Game Overview

Create a multiplayer grand strategy game set on a fictional continent based on the land shape of Europe. The coastlines, mountains, rivers, islands, and overall geography should resemble Europe so the map feels familiar, but none of the countries, borders, capitals, or cities should use real-world names. Everything should use placeholder names that can be replaced later.

The game should focus on expansion, diplomacy, economics, military strategy, and world conquest while remaining easy to learn and fast-paced.

A full match should last 45-90 minutes.

Main Menu

When players join, they enter a lobby.

From the lobby they can:

Choose a nation.

View nation information.

Invite friends.

Customize cosmetics.

Vote for game settings.

Wait for enough players before the match starts.

Nation Selection

There are 51 playable nations spread across the continent.

Every nation occupies a unique location on the map.

Players select a nation before the match begins.

Each nation displays:

Placeholder Country Name

Flag (Placeholder)

Difficulty

Starting Economy

Population

Resources

National Bonus

Capital:
Capital Alpha

Cities:

City Gamma

City Delta

Capital:
Capital Bravo

Cities:

City Echo

City Delta

City Sierra

City Omega

Every country should only use placeholder names until custom names are created later.

No real country names should appear anywhere.

Spawning

Once every player has selected a nation and the countdown ends:

Players automatically load into their nation's capital city.

The capital acts as the center of government.

Every capital contains:

Government Building

Barracks

Factory

Town Hall

Resource Storage

Spawn Point

Airport (locked early game)

Rail Station

Construction Yard

Players may freely walk around the capital while also controlling their nation through the strategy interface.

Map Design

The world is a fictional continent inspired by Europe.

The map should include:

Northern frozen regions

Western islands

Large mountain ranges

Central plains

Southern peninsulas

Eastern forests

Major rivers

Large lakes

Surrounding oceans

Although the terrain resembles Europe, every border is fictional.

No real borders should be copied exactly.

Provinces

Each nation contains several provinces.

Each province includes:

Population

Income

Infrastructure

Natural Resources

Defense

Happiness

Some provinces contain cities.

Others are farmland or wilderness.

Capturing provinces expands national territory.

Capitals

Every nation starts with exactly one capital.

The capital:

Produces the highest income.

Contains government buildings.

Acts as the nation's respawn point.

Stores national resources.

Can recruit every military unit.

If a capital is captured:

Production decreases.

National morale drops.

Income is reduced.

If the capital is recaptured, these penalties are removed.

Cities

Each nation contains multiple cities besides the capital.

City names are placeholders only.

City Charlie

City Delta

City Orion

City Zenith

Players construct:

Factories

Research Centers

Farms

Power Plants

Harbors

Airfields

Hospitals

Police Stations

Fortresses

Buildings upgrade through multiple levels.

Higher levels greatly improve production.

Military

Military branches include:

Infantry

Mechanized Infantry

Heavy Infantry

Engineers

Tanks

Rocket Vehicles

Special Forces

Aircraft

Naval Fleets

Support Vehicles

Each unit has strengths and weaknesses.

Armies automatically fight when enemy forces meet.

Players influence battles using tactical abilities rather than controlling every soldier.

Diplomacy

Players may:

Declare War

Offer Peace

Create Alliances

Trade Resources

Share Intelligence

Guarantee Independence

Request Military Access

Send Financial Aid

Negotiate Treaties

Technology

Research categories:

Industry

Military

Construction

Agriculture

Medicine

Transportation

Communications

Energy

Only one technology may be researched at a time.

Completing research permanently improves the nation.

Public Happiness

Every nation tracks happiness.

High happiness provides:

Better income

Faster production

Higher recruitment

Greater stability

Low happiness causes:

Riots

Lower tax income

Reduced production

Possible rebellions

Victory Conditions

Players can win by:

Conquering the entire continent.

Owning the largest economy.

Completing all research.

Leading the strongest alliance.

title: Upstream P0120 — deathmatch_shooter
prompt:
I've always wanted to create a Roblox game that feels completely different from every other shooter on the platform. Instead of bright arcade-style gameplay with unrealistic movement, my goal is to build a first-person multiplayer tactical shooter that feels immersive, intense, and realistic while still being fun for Roblox players.

The game is set in a modern world where players join elite military units, special response teams, or private operators. Every match is designed to feel like a real operation instead of a simple team deathmatch. Players will need to communicate, plan strategies, and work together to accomplish objectives such as rescuing hostages, planting or defusing explosives, capturing intelligence, or eliminating enemy forces.

One of the biggest features I want is an advanced physics system. Every weapon should feel unique with realistic recoil patterns, weight, and handling. Bullets won't simply hit instantly-they will travel at realistic speeds, allowing for bullet drop over long distances, wall penetration through thinner materials, ricochets on metal surfaces, and suppression effects that make nearby bullets terrifying even when they miss. Explosions will create shockwaves that move nearby objects, break windows, and throw debris across the battlefield.

The environments will be highly detailed and interactive. Players can breach doors with explosives or shotguns, shoot lights to create darkness, destroy fences, climb through windows, and use the environment to gain tactical advantages. Buildings won't be completely destructible, but certain walls, barricades, furniture, and cover can be damaged or destroyed during firefights, forcing players to constantly adapt.

Movement is another major focus. Instead of fast arcade movement, players will have realistic animations for walking, sprinting, crouching, leaning around corners, going prone, vaulting over obstacles, climbing ladders, and sliding into cover. Every action should feel smooth and responsive while maintaining a sense of weight. Equipment carried by players affects movement speed, encouraging different playstyles.

Weapons will be fully customizable. Players can attach scopes, suppressors, flashlights, lasers, grips, extended magazines, stocks, and different ammunition types. Each attachment changes the weapon's handling, recoil, accuracy, and performance instead of simply increasing damage. Every firearm will feature detailed reload animations, realistic sounds, visible magazines, shell casings, and weapon inspections.

Sound design will play a huge role in immersion. Gunfire echoes differently depending on the environment, footsteps change depending on the surface, and players can hear distant firefights across the map. Rain, wind, thunder, and environmental effects will create a living atmosphere that keeps every match feeling different.

The game will feature multiple large maps inspired by cities, forests, mountains, industrial complexes, abandoned facilities, military bases, and villages. Dynamic weather and day-night cycles will change visibility and strategy every match. Night operations will require players to use flashlights or night vision equipment to navigate safely.

A realistic damage system makes every encounter meaningful. Instead of simply losing health, players may suffer injuries that reduce movement speed, blur vision, or affect weapon handling until treated by teammates. Medical kits, armor plates, and teamwork become essential for survival. Reviving teammates can completely change the outcome of a battle.

Vehicles will also use realistic physics. Military trucks, armored vehicles, helicopters, boats, and utility vehicles each handle differently depending on terrain, weather, and damage. Tires can burst, engines can fail, and collisions have realistic consequences.

The multiplayer experience will support large battles with up to 64 players. Ranked modes reward teamwork, communication, and objective play rather than simply getting the most eliminations. Casual playlists provide faster gameplay for players who want shorter matches.

To keep the game fair, there will be no pay-to-win mechanics. Cosmetic items such as uniforms, camouflage patterns, helmets, gloves, weapon skins, and character customization allow players to personalize their appearance without affecting gameplay. Every weapon can be unlocked through progression and skill.

My dream is for this game to become one of the most realistic first-person shooters ever made on Roblox. I want players to feel nervous before entering a building, excited when coordinating with teammates, and proud after winning a difficult objective through strategy instead of luck. Every sound, animation, explosion, and firefight should make players forget they are playing a Roblox game and instead feel like they are part of a real tactical operation. If I can achieve that level of realism, teamwork, physics, and immersion, I believe the game could become one of the most memorable multiplayer shooters on the platform.
evidence: "first-person multiplayer tactical shooter"; "real operation instead of a simple team deathmatch"; "squad-versus-squad multiplayer"; "close-quarters breaches"; and players can "breach doors" and feel "nervous before entering a building."

title: Upstream P0142 — dress_up
prompt:
Create a polished single-player dress-up game with satisfying progression and visual quality, but with an original identity (do not copy assets, UI, maps, or copyrighted content).

Core Gameplay:
- The player enters a boutique-style dressing room.
- They customize a feminine avatar using clothing, hairstyles, accessories, makeup, shoes, and colors.
- Clothing changes should happen instantly with smooth animations.
- Include categories for Tops, Bottoms, Dresses, Shoes, Hair, Accessories, Makeup, and Props.
- Every item should have high-quality thumbnails.

Progression:
- Earn coins by completing styling challenges.
- Daily login rewards.
- Unlock premium outfits through progression.
- Include achievements and collectible fashion sets.
- Allow players to save multiple outfits.

Styling Challenges:
- Random themes such as:
 - Summer Picnic
 - Cyberpunk
 - Red Carpet
 - Fairy
 - Cottagecore
 - Y2K
 - Dark Academia
 - Streetwear
 - Beach Vacation
- The game scores the outfit based on matching tags assigned to clothing items.
- Display a detailed score breakdown and reward coins.

Environment:
- Cozy luxury fashion studio.
- Modern boutique with warm lighting.
- Dressing room mirrors.
- Runway area to preview finished outfits.
- Photo booth where players can take screenshots with different backgrounds and poses.

UI:
- Minimal, elegant interface.
- Pink, cream, gold, and white color palette.
- Large buttons optimized for mobile.
- Smooth transitions and animations.
- Outfit categories on the left, item grid on the right.
- Coin counter, settings, and wardrobe save slots.

Technical Requirements:
- Organize the project cleanly with reusable modules.
- Use performant scripting suitable for mobile devices.
- Placeholder clothing assets are acceptable if necessary.
- Create scalable systems so hundreds of clothing items can be added later.

Future Expansion:
- Prepare systems for multiplayer fashion competitions.
- Seasonal events.
- Limited-time collections.
- Premium currency.
- Fashion passes.
- Pets and companions.

Start by building:
1. The boutique map.
2. The avatar customization system.
3. Outfit saving.
4. Currency system.
5. One complete clothing collection with around 50 placeholder items.
6. One working styling challenge.

title: Upstream P0145 — dress_up
prompt:
Runway Royale - A Fully 3D Fashion Experience

The moment players join Runway Royale, they step into a breathtaking 3D fashion city filled with towering glass buildings, glowing fountains, moving digital billboards, palm trees swaying in the breeze, and luxury boutiques stretching in every direction. The world feels alive, with birds flying overhead, music echoing through the streets, and NPC fashion models walking around.

At the center of the city is a massive circular runway plaza where every fashion show takes place. Surrounding it are beautiful stores, cafés, photo spots, gardens, and portals leading to different fashion experiences.

Every player has their own private 3D dressing booth. Sliding glass doors close behind them, giving them a stylish space with floor-to-ceiling mirrors, adjustable lighting, makeup stations, clothing racks, rotating platforms, and shelves displaying shoes, handbags, jewelry, and accessories. Players can walk around the booth naturally, zoom in to style details, save outfits, and decorate the room with themes they unlock.

The non-VIP fashion district is enormous, with multiple clothing stores connected by wide streets. Each shop specializes in different styles such as casual, formal, fantasy, sportswear, vintage, beachwear, streetwear, and seasonal fashion. Players physically walk through each boutique, browsing clothing displayed on mannequins and shelves before instantly trying it on.

VIP members unlock access to an exclusive luxury district hidden behind elegant golden gates. Inside are marble floors, sparkling crystal chandeliers, indoor waterfalls, floating displays, and designer collections unavailable anywhere else. Premium gowns shimmer as players move, wings glow softly, accessories sparkle, and exclusive hairstyles feature beautiful animated details. VIP players also enjoy private runways, luxury dressing suites, and relaxing lounges overlooking the city.

Each fashion round begins with a randomly selected theme. Players have five minutes to explore the stores, create the perfect outfit, and add makeup, hairstyles, and accessories before heading to the runway.

The runway itself is a giant 3D stage with moving lights, giant LED screens, smoke effects, fireworks, floating platforms, and dynamic backgrounds that change with every theme. Spotlights follow each model as they confidently walk down the catwalk, strike poses, and show off every angle of their outfit while the audience cheers.

Players vote based on creativity, styling, theme accuracy, and overall presentation. Winners stand on a grand podium while confetti falls, fireworks explode above the city, and giant screens display their names and outfits for everyone to admire.

Outside of competitions, players can explore the city, complete fashion quests, discover hidden collectibles, decorate their dressing booths, take photos in scenic locations, trade accessories, unlock achievements, level up through fashion ranks, and participate in seasonal events that transform the entire world with new decorations, clothing collections, and limited-time experiences.

Runway Royale isn't just a dress-up game-it's a living 3D fashion world where players can explore, create, compete, and express their style in a vibrant city that feels exciting every time they visit.

Create a polished multiplayer Roblox horror game called "Yourself." The main enemy is a dark, corrupted version of the player called Yourself. Lobby

- A lobby similar to "99 Nights in the Forest."
- Players can create or join rooms.
- Each room supports 1-4 players.
- The host can start the game.
- All players in the room are teleported together.

Objective

Escape from a large maze.

- Find 5 Key Fragments scattered around the maze.

- After collecting all five fragments, they automatically combine into a complete key.
- Use the completed key to unlock the exit gate.

Maze

- Large maze with random dead ends.
- Dark atmosphere.
- Fog.
- Flickering lights.
- Creepy ambient sounds.
- Small rooms and hiding spots.

Yourself

The monster is called Yourself.

Appearance:

- Looks exactly like a Roblox player.
- Entire body is pure black.
- Glowing white eyes.
- No visible facial features other than the eyes.
- Smooth walking and chasing animations.

Behavior:

- Randomly appears near players.
- Chases one player for 10 seconds.
- Runs slightly slower than a player's normal sprint speed.
- When the chase begins, the targeted player receives a temporary speed boost, making escape possible.
- Disappears after 10 seconds if the chase ends.

Final Phase

When the fifth Key Fragment is collected:

- The maze turns dark red.
- Emergency alarms begin.
- The background music becomes much more intense.
- Yourself permanently spawns.
- Yourself continuously hunts all remaining players until they escape or die.
- The exit gate unlocks.

Multiplayer

- Supports 1-4 players.
- Players remain together from the lobby.
- The game ends if everyone dies.
- Escaping through the exit counts as a win.

Visual Style

- Roblox horror graphics.
- Realistic lighting.
- Heavy shadows.
- Volumetric fog.
- High-quality sound effects.
- Smooth animations.
- Optimized performance for multiplayer.

The game should gradually build tension before ending with an intense escape sequence where Yourself relentlessly hunts every remaining player.

title: Upstream P0193 — exploration
prompt:
Game Name (working title)
LAST ROUTE
"No one knows why the road is still open."
Core Idea
You and up to 5 friends are driving one truck across a frozen mountain to deliver the last generator core to a dying town.
Without it...
Thousands of people freeze.
So turning back isn't an option.
Core Gameplay Loop
Drive ⬇ Reach checkpoint ⬇ Random event ⬇ Solve it together ⬇ Repair truck ⬇ Continue ⬇ Repeat ⬇ Final escape
The truck almost never stops for long. The journey is the game.
The BIG Hook
The Storm Changes Every Run.
Not just weather.
The storm changes the world.
Examples:
🌨 Heavy snow.
Visibility 5 metres.
🧊 Frozen lake.
Road disappears.
Drive over ice.
Risk breaking through.
🌲 Fallen trees.
Need axes.
⛰ Avalanche.
New road opens.
Old road closes.
📡 Strange radio signal.
Follow it...
Or ignore it.
🏚 Abandoned village appears.
Sometimes.
Not every run.
Every run feels different.
Player Jobs
Everyone naturally gets a role.
🚛 Driver
Can only focus on driving.
🗺 Navigator
Uses map.
Finds routes.
Reads signs.
🔧 Mechanic
Repairs truck.
Keeps engine alive.
Changes tyres.
📦 Scavenger
Searches buildings.
Gets fuel.
Food.
Medicine.
Parts.
🔦 Lookout
Uses binoculars.
Warns about danger.
Nobody is standing around.
The Horror
No zombie waves.
No screaming monster.
Something...
Is following the truck.
It never attacks directly.
Instead...
Fuel disappears.
Doors open.
Lights go out.
Tyre tracks appear beside yours.
Someone knocks...
But nobody is there.
The mystery is the horror.
Mid Game Twist
You discover...
Every abandoned truck looks exactly like yours.
Same number.
Same cargo.
Same scratches.
How?
Nobody knows.
Now players start theorising.
Final Act
The storm gets insane.
Truck barely works.
Visibility almost zero.
Radio cuts in.
Someone says...
"Don't let it overtake you."
Now everyone panics.
You don't even know what "it" is.
Ending
Reach the town.
Unload generator.
Lights come on.
Storm instantly stops.
Outside...
Your truck has six sets of footprints around it.
Nobody says anything.
Game ends.
Players immediately start discussing what happened.
Why I think this is stronger
The mystery is what people remember.
Not:
"Big monster killed me."
But:
"WHY WAS THERE ANOTHER TRUCK?"
Those kinds of mysteries create YouTube theory videos.
MVP (cheap version)
One truck.
One mountain road.
Three checkpoints.
10-15 random events.
One ending.
No giant open world.
No massive AI.
The game could be finished in about 20-30 minutes per run.
But here's the one thing I'd still change.
I wouldn't make it a pure horror game.
I'd make it 70% adventure, 30% horror.
If players are scared the whole time, the fear wears off. If most of the game is about teamwork, driving, and making decisions, then the strange moments hit much harder because they're unexpected.
One last thing: if your goal is a viral Roblox game, don't try to beat Dead Rails by adding more monsters or more mechanics. Beat it by making players ask one question after every run:
"Wait... what actually happened out there?"
That kind of mystery gives people a reason to replay, tell their friends, and watch theory videos. That's much harder to copy than just another survival game.
evidence: "One compact region-scale mountain road with all three checkpoints along it" and "No giant open world" support a contained route rather than separate maps or a biome-scaled world.

Reads signs.

Changes tyres.

Searches buildings.
Gets fuel.

Medicine.
Parts.

Warns about danger.

No zombie waves.
No screaming monster.

Fuel disappears.
Doors open.
Lights go out.
Tyre tracks appear beside yours.
Someone knocks...

The mystery is the horror.

You discover...
Every abandoned truck looks exactly like yours.
Same number.
Same cargo.
Same scratches.
How?
Nobody knows.
Now players start theorising.
Final Act
The storm gets insane.
Truck barely works.
Visibility almost zero.
Radio cuts in.
Someone says...
"Don't let it overtake you."
Now everyone panics.
You don't even know what "it" is.
Ending
Reach the town.
Unload generator.
Lights come on.
Storm instantly stops.
Outside...
Your truck has six sets of footprints around it.
Nobody says anything.
Game ends.
Players immediately start discussing what happened.
Why I think this is stronger
The mystery is what people remember.
Not:
"Big monster killed me."
But:
"WHY WAS THERE ANOTHER TRUCK?"
Those kinds of mysteries create YouTube theory videos.

One truck.
One mountain road.
Three checkpoints.
10-15 random events.
One ending.

prompt:
Creating a planet called Frost Nova for a Roblox exploration game sounds like a fantastic project! Since your theme is "ruins and relics," you can lean into a "Frozen Civilization" aesthetic.

Here is a breakdown of how to design and build Frost Nova:

1. The Visual Concept (The "Nova" look)

The name "Frost Nova" suggests something more intense than just a regular ice planet. Think of it as a planet that was once a sun or a tropical paradise that was instantly flash-frozen.

Color Palette: Deep navy blues, piercing cyan, and glowing white. Use neon parts sparingly to represent "Frozen Energy."
Terrain: Instead of just flat snow, use the Roblox Terrain Editor to create jagged "Ice Spikes" (Glacial formations) and deep ravines. Use the Ice and Snow materials, but mix in Basalt for the dark, rocky ground beneath the ice.
Atmosphere: Go to Lighting > Atmosphere . Set the Density higher to create a foggy blizzard effect, and set the Color to a light blue to make the air feel cold.

2. The Ruins (Where the relics are)

Since the game is about ruins, you want the structures to look like they were swallowed by the frost.

The "Shattered Observatory": A massive dome made of "SmoothPlastic" (simulating ancient stone) that has been cracked open by giant ice crystals growing through it.
Frozen Hallways: Use "Glass" material with high transparency and a blue tint to create walls of ice that have ancient carvings visible inside them.
Mechanic Idea: Maybe players have to use a "Heat Lantern" tool to melt thin ice barriers to enter the ruins.

3. The Relics (The loot)

To fit the "Frost Nova" theme, the relics should feel cold or energetic.

The Glacial Heart: A pulsing blue crystal that hums.
Nova Shards: Fragments of the planet's original core, which could be used to upgrade the player's cold-resistance gear.
Cryo-Scrolls: Ancient documents frozen in blocks of ice that tell the story of how the planet became Frost Nova.

4. Roblox Technical Tips

Particle Effects: Create a ParticleEmitter in a large transparent part over the whole map. Use a small white circle texture with a bit of "Transparency" and "Speed" to create a falling snow effect.
Environment Sounds: Search the Roblox Creator Store for "Wind Howl" or "Ice Cracking" sounds. Set them to Looped = true to build the atmosphere.
Lighting Effects: Add a ColorCorrectionEffect in Lighting and slightly increase the Saturation and Contrast to make the blue crystals really pop against the white snow.

title: Upstream P0201 — exploration
prompt:
Create a Roblox game called Echofall.
Genre: Multiplayer Adventure, Exploration, Survival and Social Strategy.
The map is a massive floating world made of islands connected by bridges, caves, forests, snowy mountains, volcanoes, deserts and ancient ruins.
Every new server starts with the exact same peaceful world.
Hidden in the game is an invisible system called "The Echo."
Every player action adds points to different Echo categories:
• Fighting increases Chaos. • Building increases Civilization. • Exploring increases Discovery. • Helping players increases Harmony. • Destroying nature increases Corruption.
Every five minutes, whichever category is strongest permanently changes the server.
Examples:
Chaos creates stronger monsters, meteor showers and dangerous weather.
Harmony creates healing springs, friendly creatures and safe villages.
Civilization causes NPCs to build towns, roads and trading posts.
Discovery reveals secret caves, floating islands and hidden bosses.
Corruption slowly transforms forests into dark biomes with unique loot.
None of these events are announced beforehand. Players only notice the world changing around them.
Every server develops differently depending on its players.
Add over 150 random world events.
Examples include:
Giant walking castles.
Dragon migrations.
Ancient doors opening.
Floating whales flying through the sky.
Eclipse events.
Treasure storms.
Underground kingdoms appearing.
Living forests.
Crystal rain.
Giant sea monsters.
Every event should be rare and unpredictable.
Players begin with nothing.
Progress by crafting equipment, discovering recipes, unlocking abilities, collecting pets and earning Echo powers.
Instead of traditional levels, players gain Reputation from exploration, teamwork and achievements.
Reputation unlocks cosmetics, titles, mounts and emotes instead of stronger weapons.
Hidden around the world are mysterious Echo Relics.
When enough relics are activated together, the entire server enters a unique Endgame State.
There should be at least 20 different Endgame States, each completely transforming the world.
Examples:
Eternal Night.
Sky Kingdom.
Frozen World.
Machine Civilization.
Ocean Planet.
Monster Dominion.
Ancient Gods Return.
Every Endgame State has exclusive bosses, loot, music, weather and visual effects.
Add dynamic music that changes depending on the world's condition.
Include day/night cycles, realistic weather, seasons and natural disasters.
Create highly detailed environments with vibrant lighting, particles and cinematic effects.
Design every creature with unique behaviours instead of simple attacks.
NPCs should remember player actions and react differently based on reputation.
Add hidden puzzles requiring multiple players to solve together.
Include thousands of collectible items, hundreds of armour sets, rare mounts, pets, emotes, titles and visual cosmetics.
Keep all gameplay fair with no pay-to-win mechanics.
Monetisation should only include cosmetics, pets, visual effects, animations, emotes and premium housing decorations.
Optimise the game for mobile, console and PC with smooth performance.
The goal is to create a world where every server tells a completely different story, encouraging players to return because they never know what adventure will happen next.

title: Upstream P0206 — idle
prompt:
Build a simple Roblox game called Sword Chest: Idle Collector.

IMPORTANT:
Keep the first version extremely simple.
Build only the core gameplay loop described below.
Use simple Roblox parts and basic UI.
Make the full game functional and playable before adding visual polish.

GAME IDEA

The player collects coins automatically, spends coins opening treasure chests, receives random swords, and equips stronger swords to increase how many coins they earn.

CORE LOOP

1. Player earns coins automatically.
2. Player spends coins to open a chest.
3. The chest gives the player one random sword.
4. The sword is added to the player's inventory.
5. The player can equip the sword.
6. Equipped swords increase coins earned per second.
7. Better swords help the player afford better chests.
8. Better chests contain stronger and rarer swords.
9. Save all progress between sessions.

STARTING PLAYER DATA

Each new player starts with:

- 100 Coins
- 1 Coin per second
- No swords
- No equipped sword

MAIN WORLD

Create one small fantasy room.

The room should contain five treasure chests arranged from left to right:

1. Wooden Chest
2. Silver Chest
3. Golden Chest
4. Platinum Chest
5. Diamond Chest

Place a sign above each chest showing:

- Chest name
- Chest price
- Possible sword rarities

The player should walk up to a chest and use a ProximityPrompt to open it.

CHEST PRICES

Wooden Chest:
- Cost: 100 Coins

Silver Chest:
- Cost: 500 Coins

Golden Chest:
- Cost: 2,500 Coins

Platinum Chest:
- Cost: 12,500 Coins

Diamond Chest:
- Cost: 50,000 Coins

OPENING A CHEST

When the player activates a chest:

1. Check whether the player has enough coins.
2. If not, show: "You need more coins!"
3. If the player has enough coins, subtract the chest price.
4. Play a short chest-opening animation.
5. Select a random sword from that chest's loot table.
6. Show the sword in the center of the screen.
7. Display its name, rarity, and coin bonus.
8. Add it to the player's inventory.
9. Show two buttons:
 - Equip
 - Close

The chest-opening animation should take approximately one second.

SWORD RARITIES

Use these rarities:

- Common
- Uncommon
- Rare
- Epic
- Legendary
- Mythic

Use matching UI colors:

- Common: gray
- Uncommon: green
- Rare: blue
- Epic: purple
- Legendary: orange
- Mythic: bright pink or red

CHEST LOOT CHANCES

WOODEN CHEST

title: Upstream P0211 — incremental_simulator
prompt:
Gameplay Loop:
You are building a grid-based incremental game called "Mushroom Manager". In Mushroom Manager, players are given a 8x8 grid that they place mushrooms onto. The goal of Mushroom Manager is to gain spores, a currency generated by placed mushrooms every second. There are 5 mushroom variations: Basic Shrooms generate 1 spore per second, Fever Shrooms make adjacent mushrooms generate 2x spores (effect can stack), Radio Shrooms increase the range of mushrooms with AoE effects like fever shrooms or other radio shrooms, Shy Shrooms generate 10 spores per second but generate none if adjacent to another mushroom, and Pop Shrooms generate 1 spore per second but when popped they active the pop effect 10 times instead of once. Every second, any placed mushroom has a 10% chance to become "poppable", highlighting it in yellow. Poppable shrooms can be clicked to immediately generate it's current spore amount * 10. Each mushroom type has a base cost of 10 spores, but placing the mushroom then makes the next mushroom of the same type cost 2x as much.

UI/UX: The game supports 8 players at a time, with claimable plots. Players are assigned a plot automatically upon joining. The plots contain the 8x8 playing grid, which is a green checkerboard of 4x4x4 grass material blocks. Players will see their name and avatar on a billboard in front of their plot. The shroom inventory is accessed at the bottom of the screen, displaying all mushroom types. Players can press a mushroom to select it, and then click on a grid part to place it. Alternatively, they can drag from the button and onto the grid to place it. Mushroom buttons display their current cost. If a player right clicks a mushroom (or long presses on mobile), that mushroom is deleted and the cost for that mushroom type is cut in half.

Aesthetics:
The game uses a classic, blocky Roblox aesthetic. Basic mushrooms are blue and plain. Fever shrooms are red and themed around fire. Radio Shrooms look like a satellite dish. Shy Shrooms are normal sized when active, but tiny when inactive. Pop Shrooms look like they have additional heads coming out of the main head. When Mushrooms are active on the grid, they grow and shrink in size slightly for a bouncy effect.Shrooms display how many spores they're generating over their mesh when the mouse hovers over it or the player is nearby. Popping a shroom causes the shroom to briefly grow in size with an elastic like effect, before springing back to size. Poppable shrooms are highlighted when poppable. Throughout the game, it is a priority to include fun vfx and sfx for every interaction. Interactions with UI, shrooms, etc. must always have vfx/sfx for actions such as hover, click, etc. when relevant.

prompt:
Game Design Doc - "Aether Roll" (3D RNG Aura Collector)
Target platform: Roblox (Luau). Rendering: Fully 3D world with a third-person camera. This is NOT a 2D or GUI-only game - the player controls an avatar walking through explorable 3D biomes. UI overlays sit on top of the 3D world.
Genre: Incremental / RNG collector, inspired by Sol's RNG and similar "rolling" games. Core loop is roll → collect rare auras → boost luck → chase rarer auras.

1. Core Concept
The player controls a 3D avatar in an explorable world. They press a Roll button to generate a random cosmetic Aura (a particle/visual effect attached to their character) drawn from a weighted rarity table. Rarer auras are astronomically unlikely. The player increases their Luck stat over time (via gear, potions, quests, and biomes) to improve odds, and collects auras in an inventory. There is no combat requirement to progress - the chase itself is the game.
Auras are purely cosmetic and confer no combat power; their value is rarity and appearance. This is intentional and central to the design.

2. The 3D World
The world is a single explorable place composed of connected zones. Build it in 3D with real Parts/terrain, not menus.
 • Spawn Hub - central area where the player begins. Contains the roll station platform, NPC vendors, and paths to other zones.
 • Biomes - distinct 3D environments the world cycles through (see §6). Each has its own skybox, lighting, terrain, ambient audio, and particle weather. Biomes change globally on a timer for all players in the server.
 • Crafting area - a building/room containing the crafting workbench NPC.
 • Explorable paths - walkable terrain connecting zones, with collectible nodes scattered around (materials for crafting).
The avatar is standard Roblox R15. The equipped aura renders as attached ParticleEmitters / Beams / Trails and dynamic lighting on the character, visible in the 3D world to all players.

3. Core Loop
 1 Player walks avatar to (or is anywhere near) the roll station.
 2 Player presses Roll (button on screen, or auto-roll toggle).
 3 A short 3D roll animation plays (character glows, effect builds).
 4 Server computes the result from the weighted table using current Luck.
 5 Result aura is revealed with a reveal effect scaled to rarity (screen shake, sound sting, server-wide announcement for top-tier rolls).
 6 Aura is added to inventory; player may equip it.
 7 Player spends downtime raising Luck (potions, gear, quests, moving to favorable biomes), then rolls again.
Roll speed is a stat. Base cooldown ~1s; gear and gamepasses reduce it. Auto-roll repeatedly rolls on cooldown while the player is AFK.

4. Rarity & Luck System (server-authoritative)
All RNG must run on the server. The client only requests a roll and displays the result. Never trust client-reported results.
Rarity tiers
Use a tiered table. Each aura has a base "1 in N" chance. Suggested tier bands (tune later):
Tier
Base odds range
Example count
Common
1 in 2 - 1 in 10
many
Uncommon
1 in 10 - 1 in 100
many
Rare
1 in 100 - 1 in 1,000
~20
Epic
1 in 1k - 1 in 10k
~15
Legendary
1 in 10k - 1 in 1M
~10
Mythic
1 in 1M - 1 in 100M
~6
Transcendent
1 in 100M - 1 in 3B
~5
Event / Craft-only
separate pools
varies
Luck calculation
Store each aura as a base weight (higher weight = more common). Luck reduces the effective threshold for rare auras. A workable model:
Luck = ((1 + BaseLuck) * RollMultiplier + SpecialLuck) * VIPMultiplier
Rolling algorithm (list-search style, matching the genre):
 1 Build the roll pool of all auras available in the current biome/event.
 2 Sort candidates from rarest to most common.
 3 For each candidate, effective chance = baseChance / Luck (higher Luck → rarer things become attainable).
 4 Roll a random number per candidate in rarity order; first one that "hits" is awarded. If none hit, award a common fallback.
Luck sources stack: equipped gear (glove/device), active potions (multiplicative), biome multipliers (biome-exclusive auras and discounts), VIP gamepass, and a "every Nth roll gives 2x luck" pity mechanic for early-game feel.
Keep a config table (ModuleScript) of all auras: {id, name, tier, baseChance, biomeExclusive?, craftOnly?, vfxConfig} so content is data-driven and easy to extend.

5. Auras (cosmetic rewards)
Each aura is a visual effect package applied to the avatar in 3D:
 • ParticleEmitters (color, texture, rate, size over lifetime)
 • Optional PointLight / colored character glow
 • Optional Trail/Beam
 • Optional custom sound loop while equipped
 • Rarer auras = more elaborate, multi-layered effects and unique colors.
Player can equip one aura at a time (or allow a small loadout later). Equipped aura is replicated so other players see it. Inventory stores counts of each rolled aura.
Start with ~40-60 auras across tiers for launch; the data-driven table makes adding more trivial.

6. Biomes
Biomes are timed global world-states affecting the 3D environment and the roll pool.
 • The server picks the active biome on a schedule (e.g., rotate every 5-10 min, with rare biomes on low probability).
 • Each biome: changes Lighting (ClockTime, ambient, fog), skybox, weather particles, and applies a luck/roll modifier plus unlocks biome-exclusive auras.
 • Announce biome changes server-wide with an on-screen banner and sound.
 • Examples: Normal, Windy (minor luck boost), Rainy, Snowy, Starfall (rare, big luck boost + exclusive auras), Corruption/Null (very rare, exclusive high-tier auras).
Biome transitions should animate (lighting tween, particles fade in) rather than snap.

7. Crafting
At a 3D workbench NPC, players convert collected auras + materials into gear/potions or craft-only auras (guaranteed top-tier route bypassing pure RNG).
 • Gear (gloves/devices): permanent Luck and/or roll-speed boosts while equipped. Higher recipes = bigger boosts.
 • Potions: temporary Luck multipliers (timed buffs); consumed on use, stack multiplicatively.
 • Craft-only auras: require multiple rare ingredients; a guaranteed path to a prestige aura.
 • Wildcard ingredient (optional): substitutes for a missing recipe component.
Recipes are data-driven config. Crafting UI is a screen overlay opened by interacting with the workbench in 3D.

8. Progression Systems
 • Quests - an NPC gives objectives ("roll 100 times", "collect a Rare aura", "visit the Starfall biome"). Rewards: coins, potions, materials. Data-driven quest table.
 • Currency (Coins) - earned from quests/achievements; spent at shop NPCs on gear, potions, storage upgrades.
 • Inventory storage - upgradable cap on how many auras can be stored.
 • Achievements - milestone rewards (roll counts, rarity firsts) granting coins.
 • (Optional) Prestige - reset progress for permanent luck bonuses to enable long-term retention.
 • Monetization (optional gamepasses): Auto-Roll, Quick-Roll (skip animation), VIP luck multiplier, 2x luck. Keep purely convenience/cosmetic; no pay-to-win over other players since auras are cosmetic.

9. Data Persistence
 • Use DataStoreService (with a session-locking wrapper such as ProfileService/ProfileStore pattern) to persist: owned auras + counts, equipped aura, coins, gear owned/equipped, active potions, quest progress, achievements, storage level, prestige level.
 • Save on leave and on periodic autosave. Handle DataStore failures gracefully (retry, don't wipe).
 • Never store or trust roll results client-side.

10. Client / Server Architecture
 • Server (ServerScriptService): all RNG, luck math, inventory writes, crafting validation, quest completion, currency, biome scheduling, DataStore. Expose a small set of RemoteEvents/RemoteFunctions: RequestRoll, EquipAura, Craft, BuyItem, UsePotion, CompleteQuest.
 • Client (StarterPlayerScripts): input handling, camera, UI overlays, playing roll/reveal VFX and equipped-aura visuals, auto-roll loop that calls RequestRoll.
 • Shared (ReplicatedStorage): config ModuleScripts (aura table, biome table, recipe table, quest table) and enums so client and server agree on data.
 • Anti-exploit: validate every remote (cooldowns, ownership, currency checks) server-side; rate-limit RequestRoll.

11. UI (overlay on the 3D world)
Screen-space GUI on top of the 3D game:
 • Roll button + auto-roll toggle + current Luck readout + roll cooldown.
 • Inventory panel (grid of owned auras, equip button, rarity color coding).
 • Crafting panel, Shop panel, Quest tracker.
 • Active-biome banner and buff indicators.
 • Rare-roll celebration overlay + server-wide announcement feed.
UI must not replace the 3D world - the avatar and biome remain visible behind panels.

12. Build Order (suggested milestones for the agent)
 1 3D hub place with spawn, roll station, walkable avatar, third-person camera.
 2 Server-side roll system + shared aura config (start with ~10 auras across tiers) + basic reveal.
 3 Equipping auras with 3D VFX replicated to all players.
 4 Inventory + DataStore persistence.
 5 Luck stat + gear/potions + luck math.
 6 Biomes (lighting/skybox/weather + roll-pool modifiers + scheduler).
 7 Crafting workbench + recipes.
 8 Quests, currency, shop, achievements.
 9 Auto-roll, gamepasses, polish (sounds, screen shake, announcements).
 10 Balance pass on the rarity table and luck curve.

13. Key Reminders
 • It is a 3D game. Real explorable environment, third-person avatar, replicated aura VFX - not a menu simulator.
 • Auras are cosmetic only; rarity is the reward.
 • All randomness and economy logic is server-authoritative.
 • Content (auras, biomes, recipes, quests) is data-driven via config modules for easy expansion.
